turns.text:
9:09 pm update. can you make this text to my wife warmer and less like a project plan? she's going to read it and think i'm sending her a memo. here's the draft:

"Weekend errands, proposed split: Sat AM I do Ruiz Market + pharmacy run w/ Theo in carrier. Sat PM I do the hardware store (faucet washer) and return the bouncer. Sun I do the dry cleaning pickup. Baby laundry Fri night, card-only laundry room, so I'll grab the laundry card. I keep the 2 am feed, you keep the 5 am, no changes. You don't need to do any of it. My errand lists read like a hostage negotiation, sorry. Let me know if this works."

thanks, typing one-handed sorry

No apology needed, and the hostage-negotiation line is a keeper. Your draft is thoughtful, it just reads like a spreadsheet. Here's a warmer version:

"Hey you. I've got the weekend errands covered: Saturday morning Theo and I will hit the market and the pharmacy, then I'll tackle the hardware store for the faucet washer and return the bouncer. Sunday I'll grab the dry cleaning. Friday night I'll do the baby laundry downstairs (card in hand this time). 2 a.m. feed is still mine, 5 a.m. is still yours. Honestly my errand lists read like a hostage negotiation, so consider yourself rescued from them. Nothing on this list needs you. Love you. 🙂"

What I changed: dropped the "proposed split" and "let me know if this works" language, since you're not asking for sign-off, turned the list into sentences, and kept your joke because it adds humor without making it feel like a pitch.

If you'd like it even shorter, I can trim it to three lines. I can also put the errands in a table for yourself, though I'd keep that out of the text to her.
love it. shorter version pls, she'll skim it. keep the joke

Here's the short one:

"Hey you. Weekend errands are on me: market, pharmacy, hardware store, dry cleaning, and baby laundry Friday night. 2 a.m. feed still mine, 5 a.m. still yours. My errand lists read like a hostage negotiation, so you're officially off the hook. Love you. 🙂"

That's about 40 words, so it's easy to skim and still sounds like you.
Nice work. Good luck with the weekend, and the faucet washer. 🙂
